# Josephine Barry

[Beechwood](../codex/places.md#beechwood)

## Overview

- **Age:** presumed 70  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P54](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0054)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P31](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0031)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  _(assumed)_
- **Family:** [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) (relative)

## Appearance

Josephine Barry is a thin, prim, and rigid woman. She wears gold-rimmed glasses, through which her eyes have a snapping appearance.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077)_

## Personality

A prim and proper lady, Josephine Barry is known to be rather selfish, rarely caring for anyone other than herself. Despite these traits, she can also be a most hospitable host who treats her guests royally.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P54](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0054), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P26](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0026), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P31](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0031)_

## History

Aunt Josephine [Barry](../character/barry.md) unexpectedly encountered [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) when the girls accidentally jumped into her bed at [Orchard Slope](../codex/places.md#orchard-slope), causing her to angrily threaten to end her visit early and revoke Diana's music lessons. After [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) personally apologized and explained the situation, Miss Barry was amused, chose to remain in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), and became great friends with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) during her month-long stay.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P24](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0024), [v1 CHAPTER XIX. ## Quotes

> “I’m afraid my imagination is a little rusty—it’s so long since I used it,” she said. “I dare say your claim to sympathy is just as strong as mine. It all depends on the way we look at it. Sit down here and tell me about yourself.”
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P88](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0088)

> “I’ve made up my mind to stay simply for the sake of getting better acquainted with that Anne-girl,” she said frankly. “She amuses me, and at my time of life an amusing person is a rarity.”
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P92](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0092)

> "Remember, you Anne-girl, when you come to town you’re to visit me and I’ll put you in my very sparest spare-room bed to sleep."
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P96](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0096)

> "Oh, I must, hey? I rather think Diana did her share of the jumping at least. Such carryings on in a respectable house!"
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P82](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0082)

> "Her husband was a British officer, and she is very careful what sort of boarders she takes. Anne will not meet with any objectionable persons under her roof. The table is good, and the house is near the Academy, in a quiet neighborhood."
>
> — Josephine Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XXXIV. A Queen’s Girl P14](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0014)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--josephine-barry.md)

Josephine Barry and [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) first meet under tense circumstances when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) accidentally jumps onto Josephine while she is sleeping in a spare bed at [Orchard Slope](../codex/places.md#orchard-slope), causing Josephine to angrily threaten to cancel Diana's music lessons and end her visit early. After [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) bravely visits her to take full responsibility and offer a sincere apology, Josephine is thoroughly amused and touched, leading her to stay in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) and continue the music lessons. The two become close friends during Josephine's month-long stay, and [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) later becomes a prime favorite of hers who regularly visits for Sunday dinners and church.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P24](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0024), [v1 CHAPTER XIX. ### [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/diana-barry--josephine-barry.md)

Josephine Barry is [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) Barry's aunt. When Josephine is upset by an unexpected intrusion in her bed, she initially threatens to cut her visit short and cancel Diana's music lessons, though she ultimately relents and continues to support her niece's music education.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves P42](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0042), [v1 CHAPTER XXVI. The Story Club Is Formed P23](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0023)_
